analysis: Reviewed the two base_text units for fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 6862-9139). They are golden test vectors: request bodies, provider bodies, template inputs, plans with prompt_contract_id and chain_hash values, and token_ids. The patch excerpt shows the changes are one-line updates of prompt_contract_id (6bb9fb05... to 8171fec3...) and related plan/hash lines. The changed ranges at base lines 6537, 6640, 6713-6725, 7693-7701, 8291-8299 and 8716-8724 are all prompt_contract_id, prompt_token_count/chain_hash or similar plan lines. The excerpt and range map are incomplete, and the head text was not supplied, so I could not check the new values. The cases include tool_call_arguments_bridge, tool_function_extra_keys and tools, with the fixed date 2028-02-29. I found no secrets, credentials, keys, or executable code in the examined content. This is a data-only fixture change with no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, App Attest (TB-011) or the coordinator-provider WebSocket (TB-002). The content also carries no runtime trust decisions. The security-relevant link is the prompt-contract identifier that drives cache routing and prefix-cache keys (T-041, cache_routing_eligible true). Changing the contract ID should invalidate cross-version cache sharing, which is a safe direction. Open questions for integration: whether the Swift/Go code that computes the contract ID and template really changed consistently with these vectors, so the fixtures match production behavior, and whether the new template or tool-forcing text changes prompt handling in a way affecting T-041 cache isolation. Neither the code nor the head side of the fixtures was supplied, so I cannot rule these out. No finding is raised.
